clue.text: Redeploy old military leader to secure South for you

parts.note: to second someone is to transfer them temporarily to other duties

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the leader's name closes round the letter

parts.note: Juan Perón, the Argentine general and president

explanation.surface: An order to move a former general into position to hold the south, on your behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts S inside PERON; the grammatical term 'you' is the definition, not a mere pronoun link.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the pronoun addressing the listener is classed by this term.

clue.text: Impish people avoiding special ceremonial

indicators.note: avoiding says those letters keep clear of the word, so they are dropped

parts.note: sprites are mischievous fairy folk

explanation.surface: Mischievous fairies keep away from special ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops SP from SPRITES; 'ceremonial' is used as a noun, a body of ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial, as a noun, is a prescribed set of ritual observances.

clue.text: Conservative island association swapping leaders

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters of the two words, which change places

parts.note: the Isle of Wight off England's south coast
a ring is a group of people associated, often illicitly

explanation.surface: A Tory island club changes its leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping leaders' exchanges the first letters. The Isle of Wight is an English island off Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Political conservatism is placed on the right of the spectrum, so a Tory is of that wing.

clue.text: Jersey industry — or Guernsey or Alderney?

definitions.text: Jersey industry — or Guernsey or Alderney?

parts.words: Jersey industry — or Guernsey or Alderney?
parts.note: the islands seem meant, but Jersey, Guernsey and Alderney are all breeds of milk cattle, so the industry is the business of producing milk

explanation.surface: Which Channel Island owns this particular industry?
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey, Guernsey and Alderney are Channel Islands, each lending its name to a breed of milking cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk farming is the trade associated with these cattle breeds named after the islands.

clue.text: Taunt's entertaining street entertainer

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting a guest, so the word takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to jeer is to taunt

explanation.surface: A mocking heckler hosting a street performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts ST inside JEER; 's stands for has and links.
explanation.definitionFit: A court fool was a professional entertainer, amusing royalty with jokes.

clue.text: Explorer's mother quite backward in intelligence

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for quite in reverse

parts.note: all, as in all alone, means quite or completely

explanation.surface: The explorer's mother is a bit slow on information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' gives LLA, which 'in' places inside the slang word for information; gen is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan led the first expedition to circumnavigate the globe, a famous voyager.

clue.text: Container brought back full, apart from last type of acid

indicators.note: brought back means the word for container is read in reverse

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: apart from last says the final letter of the word for full is removed

parts.note: rich means full, as in a full or rich flavour

explanation.surface: A container is returned full, except for the last kind of acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns TIN into NIT; 'apart from last' takes H off RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid, HNO3, is a strong corrosive acid used in fertilizers and explosives.

clue.text: Swine ripping into poster perhaps on bus?

indicators.note: ripping into says the pig bursts inside the advertisement

parts.note: an advertisement, ad, is exemplified by a poster
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A pig tearing through a poster, maybe one on the side of a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripping into' signals the container; the question mark marks 'on bus' as one example of being on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger riding a bus is on board it.

clue.text: In Florida, Bel-Air excited to see meteor

indicators.note: In places the rearranged letters within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so the letters of the place name are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Excitement in Bel-Air, Florida, over a sighting of a meteor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes IREBAL, which 'In' sets inside the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright meteor that flares brilliantly is called by this name.

clue.text: Weapon chosen partly to provide protection for Peruvian?

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A weapon is chosen to guard a Peruvian.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a description: this cloak protects people in Peru from the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: This blanket-like cloak with a head hole, traditional in the Andes, shields its wearer from rain and cold.

clue.text: Strange beast of a tailless sort given extra protection?

indicators.note: the word for extra serves as protection, wrapping around the rest

parts.note: plus means extra, an additional thing

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter of the word for sort is cut off

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: An odd animal, a breed lacking a tail, with extra armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' docks the last letter; 'protection' has the word for extra wrapping round the rest, with 'given' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: This egg-laying, duck-billed Australian mammal is famously odd.

clue.text: Current jockey marries tart, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ignoring the odds keeps only the even-placed letters of tart

explanation.surface: A jockey weds a tart, defying the betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' leaves AT from tart; 'jockey' rearranges MARRIES plus AT.
explanation.definitionFit: An air current is a flow of moving air.

clue.text: Ruminant born when starting pistol fires?

parts.note: racers start on 'go', the moment the starting signal sounds

explanation.surface: A grazing animal born just as the starting gun goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read ONGO as 'on go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bongo is a striped forest antelope of Africa, a cud-chewing animal.

clue.text: Launch observation, arresting church workers

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the remark grips the other pieces inside

parts.note: a comment is a remark or observation
men is a common crossword word for workers or staff
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Starting remark detaining the church workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' holds MENCE inside the remark; 'church workers' is read as men plus the church, joined in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A commencement is a beginning, the start or launch of something.

clue.text: Bondage techniques father's engaged in shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the whole is read upwards
engaged in means the abbreviation for father is involved inside the word for techniques

parts.note: modes are methods or techniques
FR is the abbreviation for father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: Bondage methods a priest is caught practising are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' makes MODFRES; 'shown up' reverses it up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The status of a feudal serf was a form of servitude to the lord.

clue.text: Keen crooks not doing a thorough job

parts.note: keen, as of a wind or wit, can mean cutting
crooks are bends or angles, corners

explanation.surface: Eager crooks skimp on their work.
explanation.walkthrough: Crooks look like criminals but are bends.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking shortcuts and skimping effort.

clue.text: Blue stone needs no antique setting

indicators.note: the archaic word for no acts as the setting for the stone, as in jewellery

parts.note: nay is an old-fashioned word for no
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A blue gemstone needs no setting of antique style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' makes the archaic no surround the abbreviation. A stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are smutty, as are obscene ones, so the two adjectives overlap.

clue.text: Eg. mum's unearned income supporting dad

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath the other piece

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
rental income comes in without labour

explanation.surface: Mum's income from letting, propping up dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts RENTAL below PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother's role or care is the kind belonging to a mother or father.

clue.text: Bit of jazz, a typical Indian piece

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime, an early jazz style

explanation.surface: A snatch of jazz, a characteristic Indian composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional melodic framework for improvisation in Indian classical music.

clue.text: Selected to play — second fiddle?

definitions.meaning: a secondary job or affair, as a sideline

explanation.walkthrough: Second fiddle suggests a minor role, here something done in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being picked for a team means in it; a sideline is a secondary extra.

clue.text: A sporting voice broadcast suitable item for tea interval

indicators.note: broadcast as scattering, so the letters are spread and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports commentator on air recommends a snack for the tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: The tea interval is the break in a day of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: This jam-filled sponge cake is a classic afternoon tea cake.

clue.text: Upstanding kid detained by spies spotted poisoner, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means the letters read upwards
detained by means held inside the word for spies

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
to rag is to tease or kid

explanation.surface: An upright child held by spies after spotting a poisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detained by' makes CIRAGA, which 'Upstanding' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The fly agaric, red with white spots, is a poisonous mushroom.

clue.text: Runs into the French quarter at a leisurely pace

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a ghetto is a city quarter
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Running into the French district at a relaxed speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places the runs abbreviation between the article and the quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning fairly slowly, a little faster than largo.

clue.text: Firm, lean irregular soldier

indicators.note: irregular says the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm, lean irregular fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' signals the anagram; it looks like an irregular soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantryman armed with a rifle.

clue.text: Suit to turn up with length not right

indicators.note: L for length replaces R for right

parts.note: to appear is to turn up

explanation.surface: Suit for turning up with a length not right.
explanation.walkthrough: L (length) replaces R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: To be attractive to someone is to suit them.

clue.text: Attack in anger and don't stint

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to strike out angrily and to splash out money.

clue.text: Board members finally leaving firm

indicators.note: leaving says that letter departs from the word for firm

parts.note: stable means firm or steady

indicators.note: finally picks the end letter of the word members

explanation.surface: Board members are finally leaving the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks S, which 'leaving' removes from STABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Board and table both mean a flat surface for food, or meals.

clue.text: Main source of mineral?

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea

indicators.note: source of picks out the first letter of mineral

explanation.surface: Where does mineral mainly come from?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a seam is a source of mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is a layer of coal or ore in rock.
